svg.text: Fixed-stride LMEM slots — and the cluster window
Within one kernel every CTA has the same aligned footprint, so LMEM is a fixed partition. Slot i owns [i·stride, (i+1)·stride) for the whole kernel — nothing ever moves.
Worked example — NUM_WARPS = 8, LMEM_SIZE = 16 KB, stride = 3 KB
usable_slots_r = max m in [1, 8] with m·3 KB ≤ 16 KB → 5. Slots 5..7 exist as warp slots but can never hold a CTA.

tail remainder — unusable
A byte ring would pack this too, but only for CTAs of a
DIFFERENT size — and there are none. See the note below.
LMEM_SIZE = 1 << VX_CFG_LMEM_LOG_SIZE
cta_csrs.lmem_addr = VX_MEM_LMEM_BASE_ADDR
| (base_slot * stride)
The multiply is latched at accept into cur_lmem_base_r —
off the ready path. The kernel reads it as CTA_LMEM_ADDR.
A first-of-cluster beat reserves K consecutive slots — all of them, up front
cluster_size = 3. The window must be free in its entirety before the first member is admitted, so the following K−1 members can never stall mid-cluster.

free

base 6K

base 9K
slot 4
free
The contiguity contract, in one line
member r base = issuer_base + r * stride
No per-slot base table. No receiver-side translation.
Why the stride must be block-aligned
The KMU rounds lmem_size up to MEM_BLOCK_SIZE. DXA
multicast resolves receivers by this arithmetic and LMEM is
block-addressed — a ragged stride would target the wrong block.
Pre-wrap — a window never straddles the wrap
tail_r = 3, cluster_size = 3, usable = 5. The window [3, 6) would overrun, so base_slot pre-wraps to 0 rather than splitting the cluster.
rank 0
pre-wrapped here
rank 1

slot 3
tail_r was here
slot 4
the window pre-wraps to base_slot = 0
cluster_prewrap = is_first_of_cluster
&& ((base_tail + cluster_k) > usable_slots_r)
base_tail itself normalises tail_r if a kernel change shrank usable_slots_r
K is clamped, never rejected
A cluster larger than co-residency degenerates to
cluster_k = usable_slots_r rather than deadlocking.
Co-residency is a property of the STREAM — the launch bus enforces it, not the allocator
Nothing in the dispatcher pins a cluster’s members to a core. A first-of-cluster beat reserves K slots on whichever core accepts it, and the K−1 followers land in
that window because the BUS delivers them there: a compute message is one CLUSTER, so `eop` marks its last member and every VX_kmu_bus_arb level locks its
input→output pair from the first beat to `eop`. The fan-out picks a ready core once per cluster; rr_ptr advances only on `eop`.
This is the same mechanism that keeps fragments bin→core affine — affinity that must not be load-balanced, expressed as message length. cluster_dim (1,1,1),
the default, marks every CTA `eop`: the lock never engages and the stream is the plain per-CTA round-robin, bit for bit.
Without it a follower would land on the NEXT core, take its tail slot, and the issuer’s window would go unused — a split cluster, and a barrier deadlock.
What the occupancy bound replaces
The byte ring tracked free_size in bytes and reclaimed in head order, which put
a wrap-around carry chain directly on the admission handshake.
usable_slots_r is a KERNEL CONSTANT: it changes only when the stride does, i.e.
once per launch. It is computed with a comparator tree — m·stride is a
constant-times-variable, so there is no divider anywhere in the RTL.
This is what shipping GPUs do
NVIDIA and AMD compute occupancy once at launch — max_resident_CTAs ≈
SMEM / smem_per_CTA — which is exactly a fixed per-kernel stride.
Hopper thread-block clusters address peer SMEM by rank as
peer_base = base + rank·stride. That is the same arithmetic this allocator
makes true by construction, and what DXA multicast resolves against.
